newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium wants new EU treaty "block" on enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Belgium wants new EU treaty "block" on enlargement.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Wednesday he wanted a written guarantee in the European Union's Amsterdam Treaty that no new members from eastern Europe would be admitted until its internal institutional issues were settled, Belga news agency said.

Dehaene, speaking in the Belgian parliament one day before EU foreign ministers are due to meet in Luxembourg to approve a legal version of the Amsterdam treaty, said he hoped to win the support of other EU nations for such a declaration before the treaty is formally signed in October.
EU leaders skirted the issue of institutional reform -- reducing the number of commissioners and modifying nations' voting rights -- at last week's Amsterdam Summit.
They proposed instead a protocol to the new treaty stating that institutional issues should be revisited at the time of the EU's next enlargement, expected to be around 2002.

Belga cited Dehaene as saying the contents of the protocol were "not ideal" and should be complemented by a declaration stating explicitly that enlargement could only take place once the bloc had streamlined its bureaucratic procedures.
Dehaene said he hoped Belgium would be supported in its case by Italy, the Netherlands, Finland, Austria, Portugal and Luxembourg, which assumes the EU Presidency on July 1.
A spokesman for Dehaene confirmed his remarks.
